title: The subcategory Rep_φ(G)
body_html:
The subcategory $\Rep_\phi(G)$

Setting: $G$ acts cellularly on the regular CW complex $X$, $K$ is a sheaf of subgroups of $G$ with $K_E \trianglelefteq \Fix_G(E)$ for all $E$, $R$ is a field in which the pro-orders of all $K_x$ are invertible, and $\phi = \{\phi_E\}$ is a character of $K$ (see G-equivariant (co)sheaf of subgroups and characters).

Definition. Let $\Rep(G) := \Rep_R(G)$ be the category of (smooth) $R[G]$-modules. The full subcategory $\Rep_\phi(G)$ consists of $V$ such that $$V \;=\; \sum_{x \in |X|} V[\phi_x],$$ where $V[\phi_x] := { v \in V : k \cdot v = \phi_x(k) v \text{ for all } k \in K_x }$ is the $\phi_x$-isotypic submodule. Equivalently, $V$ is generated by $\bigcup_x V[\phi_x]$.

$\Rep_\phi(G)$ is closed under taking quotient objects in $\Rep(G)$. It is a Serre subcategory under additional hypotheses (see Hypothesis (S) in Serre-subcategory property (S) — a consequence, not a hypothesis).

For the canonical example with $X = \mathcal{B}(G)$, $K = G_{\bullet, 0+}$, $\phi = \mathbf 1$, one recovers $\Rep_0(G)$ (depth-zero representations). For more general semisimple characters $\Phi = (\mathscr{K}_+, \phi)$, this becomes $\Rep_\Phi(G)$ in §7 — see The subcategory Rep_Φ(G).
